meta.title: Devlog: October 4, 2026 - October 11, 2026
meta.description: a week of product safety, clearer app support, and new windows desktop tools.

bullets.text: published a fuller bookclubr overview alongside dedicated help and privacy information, with clearer navigation from the app’s public touchpoints.

summary.text: i gave bookclubr’s public home a little more of the information it should have had from the start. less scavenger hunt, more useful context.

bullets.text: shipped updated safety controls that can block prohibited posts, limit access to removed or blocked content, and prevent suspended accounts from posting or messaging.
improved the reading-club experience with a shared book list, richer vote history, recommendations, and easier sharing of reader and club pages.
improved photo handling with better loading states, caching, and smaller uploads for reader and club images.
prepared an updated ios build for testing, while physical-device checks remain necessary before a public release.

summary.text: this was a big week of making the app feel more complete and more responsible at the same time. the public-release checklist is shorter now, but it still has a very real iphone-shaped item on it.

bullets.text: released a windows tray companion that shows active, unread, and failed codex chats at a glance.
added a searchable status view that opens matching chats while keeping monitoring read-only.
documented installation, startup, troubleshooting, and validation steps for windows users.

summary.text: i wanted a quieter way to keep an eye on codex without repeatedly opening the panel. three tiny lights felt like a reasonable answer.

bullets.text: released a standalone multi-monitor tray manager for windows, giving people control over where app and system tray items appear.
kept selected application and system icons interactive while making custom icon choices clearer.
separated monitor viewing from monitor targeting so settings can be reviewed without accidentally changing where they will be applied.
added complete configuration snapshots, an option to restore windows defaults, and a more modern manager interface.
made long icon lists easier to work through with search and added system, light, and dark appearance choices.
corrected initialization issues and improved the local development setup.

summary.text: traybridge went from a promising proof of concept to something much easier to configure without second-guessing every checkbox. windows trays are apparently a full-time hobby now.
